cases.sentence: Ростов с Ильиным в ___ выпустили на перегонку лошадей в изволок перед Богучаровым, и Ростов, перегнавший Ильина, первый вскакал в улицу деревни Богучарова.
cases.explain: «последний раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Rostóv and Ilyín gave rein to their horses for a last race along the incline before reaching Boguchárovo, and Rostóv, outstripping Ilyín, was the first to gallop into the village street.

cases.sentence: Они шагом подъехали к амбару, у которого стояла ___ мужиков.
cases.explain: «большая толпа» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: They rode at a footpace to the barn, where a large crowd of peasants was standing.

cases.sentence: Два старые, длинные мужика, с ___ и редкими бородами, вышли из кабака и с улыбками, качаясь и распевая какую-то нескладную песню, подошли к офицерам.
cases.explain: «сморщенными лицами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Some of the men bared their heads, others stared at the new arrivals without doffing their caps. Two tall old peasants with wrinkled faces and scanty beards emerged from the tavern, smiling, staggering, and singing some incoherent song, and approached the officers.

cases.explain: «небольшой мужик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “And is there a large force of you here?” said another, a short man, coming up.

cases.sentence: — Старички собрались, по ___, — отвечал мужик, отходя от него.
cases.explain: «мирскому делу» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “The old men have met to talk over the business of the commune,” replied the peasant, moving away.

cases.sentence: — Это граф Ростов, эскадронный командир, а я ваш ___.
cases.explain: «покорный слуга» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “This is Count Rostóv, squadron commander, and I am your humble servant.”

cases.sentence: — Осмелюсь беспокоить, ваше благородие, — сказал он с почтительностью, но с ___ к юности этого офицера, и заложив руку за пазуху.
cases.explain: «относительным пренебрежением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “May I make bold to trouble your honor?” said he respectfully, but with a shade of contempt for the youthfulness of this officer and with a hand thrust into his bosom. “My mistress, daughter of General in Chief Prince Nikoláy Andréevich Bolkónski who died on the fifteenth of this month, finding herself in difficulties owing to the boorishness of these people”—he pointed to the peasants—“asks you to come up to the house. … Won’t you, please, ride on a little farther,” said Alpátych with a melancholy smile, “as it is not convenient in the presence of … ?” He pointed to the two peasants who kept as close to him as horseflies to a horse.

cases.explain: «пьяных мужиков» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Ah! … Alpátych … Ah, Yákov Alpátych … Grand! Forgive us for Christ’s sake, eh?” said the peasants, smiling joyfully at him. Rostóv looked at the tipsy peasants and smiled.

cases.sentence: — сказал Яков Алпатыч с ___, не заложенною за пазуху рукой указывая на стариков.
cases.explain: «степенным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Or perhaps they amuse your honor?” remarked Alpátych with a staid air, as he pointed at the old men with his free hand.

cases.sentence: — «И какая кротость, благородство в ее чертах и в выражении!» думал он, слушая ее ___.
cases.explain: «робкий рассказ» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Princess Márya was sitting helpless and bewildered in the large sitting room, when Rostóv was shown in. She could not grasp who he was and why he had come, or what was happening to her. When she saw his Russian face, and by his walk and the first words he uttered recognized him as a man of her own class, she glanced at him with her deep radiant look and began speaking in a voice that faltered and trembled with emotion. This meeting immediately struck Rostóv as a romantic event. “A helpless girl overwhelmed with grief, left to the mercy of coarse, rioting peasants! And what a strange fate sent me here! What gentleness and nobility there are in her features and expression!” thought he as he looked at her and listened to her timid story.
